title: Sharp Non-Asymptotic Analysis of the Penalized Challenger in $\beta$-EB-TCI for Bernoulli Bandits
claim: Observed stopping times grow linearly with the confidence scale and closely match the theoretical threshold-crossing predictor, with or without guarding.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared axes, shaded bootstrap confidence bands, dashed predictor
description: Two line-plot panels sit side by side under the shared title 'Finite-confidence calibration of the stopping time'. The left panel is a separated instance (sep5) and the right is an equal-close tie class (tie-close4). Both plot stopping time on the y-axis against confidence scale log(1/δ) on the x-axis, which runs from about 9 to 18. Each panel has three series. An orange line with square markers is the unguarded algorithm. A blue line with circle markers is the guarded algorithm. A green dashed line is the predictor t_pred. Pale orange and blue shaded bands show bootstrap confidence intervals. All curves rise roughly linearly and stay close to the green dashed line. The left panel has more noise and the bands cross. The right panel is tighter, with values around 80,000 to 105,000. The legend is in the upper left.
caption: Agreement between observed stopping times and the predictor at β = 0.5. Shaded bands are bootstrap percentile 95% confidence intervals for the empirical mean over 200 replications per point. The dashed curve is the threshold-crossing predictor tpred.
abstract: Top-two algorithms are simple and effective for fixed-confidence best-arm identification, but their sharp non-asymptotic behavior is still not well understood. We study this question for Bernoulli bandits through $Î²$-EB-TCI, the empirical-best top-two rule of Jourdan et al., whose challenger minimizes a Bernoulli transportation cost plus a logarithmic penalty in its pull count. We first analyze the stabilized regime, in which the empirical leader has become the true best arm and its sampling fraction stays close to $Î²$. In this regime, every suboptimal arm is sampled linearly often, and, with high probability, the stopping time is at most $T_Î²^{\star}(Î¼)\log(1/Î´)$ plus stabilization and lower-order concentration terms, with the exact fixed-$Î²$ leading coefficient. The main remaining difficulty is therefore to control when the regime is reached. For the original rule, we obtain a non-asymptotic high-probability stopping bound on every Bernoulli instance with a unique best arm. Under a finite-mean sufficient-exploration condition, the bound yields the sharp expected sample complexity; combined with the exploration result of Jourdan et al., this covers pairwise-distinct means under their tie-breaking convention. A mild forced-exploration guard, which uses only $O(\sqrt{Kt})$ pulls up to time $t$, gives a self-contained sharp expected bound for any number of arms with a unique best arm. We also identify a limitation of proof strategies that try to handle equal suboptimal means through a single index-comparison argument.
